meta.topic: The Eiffel Tower was meant to come down
meta.thesis: The Eiffel Tower was scheduled for demolition in 1909 and survived because it proved useful for radio telegraphy.
meta.visual_anchor: the Eiffel Tower in Paris as built in 1889, an iron lattice tower; the French tricolour is the only flag allowed; no other flags, emblems, logos or lettering; no identifiable real people
meta.notes: Illustrative plan. Claims cite Wikipedia (secondary, read 2026-10-20, sections named per claim); a real publication needs primary sources (the tower's operator, French archives). Two details were checked against the page and dropped because it does not say them: a '20-year permit' (the 20 years is Eiffel's income period) and 'built as the entrance arch' (the page says centrepiece). All AI beats are clearly stylised paper cut-outs with no photoreal people, so the label is on as a precaution. Beat 6 is assembled in code from beat 1's cut-out: no new generation. The budget cap is left unset on purpose: the user chooses it from the cost card.

claims.text: The Eiffel Tower was slated for dismantling in 1909.
The tower was built from 1887 to 1889 as the centrepiece of the 1889 World's Fair.
Eiffel was to receive income during the exhibition and for the next 20 years; in 1909, when it was slated for dismantling, ownership would have reverted to the City of Paris.
claims.source_name: Wikipedia, Eiffel Tower (History, Origin and Subsequent events)

claims.text: The tower was spared from scheduled demolition because of its demonstrated utility in early 20th-century science and technology, specifically radio telegraphy.
Maintenance involves applying 60 tons of paint every 7 years to prevent rust.
The tower is painted in 3 shades (the page says 'three shades').
